title: Token Pruning
summary: Remove low-value prompt content under a measured quality constraint while preserving negation, identifiers, evidence, and instructions.
overview: Token pruning reduces the text sent to a model by selecting or compressing information that contributes to the task. It can operate at document, sentence, or token level. Learned compressors estimate importance differently from simple truncation, but all pruning methods risk removing a condition or relationship the final answer needs.

Prompt-token pruning is distinct from pruning model weights or evicting attention-cache entries. Its success criterion is end-to-end task quality at a lower total cost, including the compressor itself. Exact quotations, code, structured records, numbers, and contractual language often require protected spans rather than aggressive token deletion.

production.poc: A prototype compares sentence selection, simple truncation, and a learned compressor on the same tasks.
production.production: Production marks protected spans, retains source alignment, and evaluates factual and structural preservation at several compression ratios.
production.scale: Enterprise scale routes only suitable workloads through compression and monitors quality drift, compressor latency, and total inference savings rather than token reduction alone.

components.name: Budget controller
components.role: Sets a target based on available context and the task’s tolerated information loss.

components.name: Importance scorer
components.role: Ranks passages or tokens using a documented selection method.

components.name: Protected-span policy
components.role: Preserves instructions, identifiers, negation, units, and exact-evidence requirements.

components.name: Compression stage
components.role: Produces reduced context with links to original source ranges.

components.name: Quality gate
components.role: Checks required facts and compares downstream performance with an uncompressed baseline.

flow.title: Classify the task
flow.description: Determine whether the task permits lossy context or requires exact source wording.

flow.title: Mark protected information
flow.description: Identify mandatory instructions, numbers, entity names, and evidence-critical conditions.

flow.title: Select a compression level
flow.description: Choose an evaluated ratio that meets the latency and quality budget.

flow.title: Prune with provenance
flow.description: Remove low-value content while retaining source mapping and protected spans.

flow.title: Validate the result
flow.description: Check required fields, negation, and structure before sending the compressed prompt.

flow.title: Measure total benefit
flow.description: Include compression overhead, generation cost, and error rates in the acceptance decision.

useCase.title: Summarizing repetitive contact logs
useCase.situation: A service-quality agent reviews long contact logs containing repeated greetings, routing text, and issue updates.
useCase.problem: Boilerplate consumes most of the prompt while a few resolution facts matter.
useCase.requirement: Reduce context cost without losing the customer’s issue, promised action, or unresolved status.
useCase.architecture: A compressor removes repetitive low-value spans and protects commitments, dates, and final disposition.
runtime: The pipeline marks promised follow-up and resolution statements.
It compresses repeated routing chatter and checks that protected facts remain before summarization.
useCase.failure: If pruning removes a negation that changes whether an issue was resolved, validation rejects the compressed version.
useCase.impact: Measure commitment-retention accuracy and total processing cost; a smaller prompt is not an improvement when it changes the operational meaning.

tradeoffs.cost: May produce difficult-to-audit text and semantic loss.

failures.detection: The compressed text reverses a status or condition.
failures.recovery: Protect logical operators and compare critical statements.

failures.scenario: Compression costs more than it saves
failures.detection: Added model work exceeds avoided prefill cost.

mistakes.fix: Measure task quality and total latency.
Reserve protected policy and output-contract segments.
Retain original ranges so citations remain verifiable.

whenToUse: Use for repetitive long context with clear evidence priorities.
Use when prefill cost is material.
Use when quality can be evaluated against an uncompressed baseline.
whenNotToUse: Avoid exact quotation or code-transformation tasks without protected structure.
Do not compress already short requests by default.
Avoid pruning when required evidence cannot be identified.
checklist: Distinguish prompt pruning from model compression.
Measure compressor overhead and downstream errors.
